Gestational trophoblastic disease encompasses a spectrum of proliferative disorders ranging from non-neoplastic hydatidiform moles to malignant neoplastic conditions. Each tumour entity of gestational trophoblastic disease and two tumour-like lesions have been proposed to have histological and cytological phenotypes of distinct trophoblastic cell types in the placenta {11898845}. Placental trophoblasts are generally classified into three categories: syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts, and intermediate trophoblasts. Syncytiotrophoblasts are fully matured cells responsible for most of the placental hormone production. They are multinucleated cells with large amounts of cytoplasm that are located external to the cytotrophoblast layer on the surface of the chorionic villi. Cytotrophoblasts are primitive cells most likely with a stem cell profile. They are small to medium-sized cells with a polygonal to oval shape, are mitotically active, and may rapidly proliferate. The intermediate trophoblast layer is composed of large mononuclear cells with abundant cytoplasm, classified into three subtypes {11192071}: implantation site intermediate trophoblasts are present at the implantation site, chorionic laeve intermediate trophoblasts in the chorionic membrane, and villous (trophoblastic column) intermediate trophoblasts in anchoring villi.

#13565Table #13565 presents the classification of gestational trophoblastic diseases. Hydatidiform moles, which are proliferations of villous trophoblasts, are subclassified into complete and partial moles. Invasive hydatidiform moles (which can be complete or partial) invade the uterine myometrium and/or uterine vasculature. Gestational trophoblastic tumours include gestational choriocarcinoma, placental site trophoblastic tumour, epithelioid trophoblastic tumour, and mixed trophoblastic tumour. Tumour-like trophoblastic lesions include exaggerated placental site reaction and placental site nodule/plaque. Choriocarcinoma is a trophoblastic neoplasm recapitulating the primitive cells of the previllous stage of the placenta. The intermediate trophoblast at the implantation site is the putative cell type that gives rise to placental site trophoblastic tumour and exaggerated placental site reaction, whereas the intermediate trophoblast at the chorionic laeve is the cell type found in epithelioid trophoblastic tumour and placental site nodule. Atypical placental site nodule can be a precursor lesion to epithelioid trophoblastic tumour {25675185}.
